stories.title: EU officials scrutinize TikTok’s For You algorithm
stories.summary: The European Commission claims TikTok’s For You page violates EU law by exposing users to content that harms mental health. The feature aims to get users watching videos that interest them as quickly as possible. Algorithms are instructions written by humans to exploit behavioural patterns for time spent.

stories.title: Tech giants sue to block California teen safety law
stories.summary: Meta, Google, and TikTok are suing to block a California law that restricts addictive features like infinite scroll and autoplay for users under 16. The law, which takes effect in January, aims to address a teen mental health crisis. The companies argue against the design restrictions.

stories.title: EU charges TikTok over mental health risks
stories.summary: The European Commission has charged TikTok with failing to protect users from content that may worsen eating disorders and anxiety. The regulator claims the algorithm leads vulnerable users down rabbit holes. The platform has 189 million users in the EU and is now facing a challenge to its model.

stories.title: Lawsuit links school Chromebook to psychological crisis
stories.summary: Parents of a 13-year-old girl are suing Google, alleging a school-issued Chromebook contributed to their daughter’s psychological crisis. The lawsuit claims Google is liable for the software it controls. Schools are increasingly re-evaluating technology use as concerns grow regarding its impact on student mental health.

stories.title: Google faces lawsuit over AI-powered search results
stories.summary: Parents of a 13-year-old girl have sued Google for negligence, claiming she used AI tools on a school-issued Chromebook to plan a suicide. While the school blocked specific AI apps, the lawsuit targets the AI-powered features within Google’s search engine. It is the first case of its kind.

stories.title: AI chatbot trial shows no benefit for maternal mental health
stories.summary: A yearlong trial of 400 pregnant women and new mothers found that the AI chatbot Rosie did not improve anxiety or depression. Participants using the bot had scores similar to a group that received a monthly children's book. The study was led by University of Maryland researchers.

stories.title: AI depression detection accuracy drops in large studies
stories.summary: AI models for detecting depression show lower accuracy in large populations compared to small benchmark tests. While small studies report up to 100 percent accuracy, performance drops significantly in cohorts of several hundred to 15,000 individuals. Large-scale validation remains a challenge for these diagnostic tools.

stories.summary: A psychiatric investigation conducted at a specialized anxiety clinic in Tokyo has revealed that anxious depressive attacks represent a highly prevalent and clinically complex symptom pattern affecting more than one-fifth of newly presenting psychiatric outpatients. stories.title: Nearly 1 in 5 young Americans use AI for mental health advice
stories.summary: A RAND survey found that 8.2 million Americans aged 12 to 21 use AI for mental health information. Health professionals are raising concerns about the risks of relying on chatbots for psychiatric diagnoses and treatment. The trend is becoming increasingly common among adolescents and young adults.

stories.title: Monaural beats in music may reduce anxiety
stories.summary: Adding monaural beats to music reduced anxiety more than music alone in two online experiments with 466 participants. The study, led by researchers at Universal Music Group and Delft University, found a caveat: if the beats were too loud, the benefit vanished and reversed.

stories.title: Intensive breathwork linked to psychedelic-like effects
stories.summary: Intensive breathing exercises can induce psychedelic experiences by altering brain network communication. MRI scans showed that while breathwork reduced brain blood flow by 45 percent, the depth of the experience did not correlate with the drop in blood supply. The brain changes how it talks to itself.

stories.title: Irregular sleep linked to heart disease
stories.summary: Research analyzing data from more than 10,000 U.S. adults suggests that inconsistent bedtimes and wake-up times can harm heart health, even when total sleep duration is sufficient. The findings indicate that sleep regularity may be as important for cardiovascular protection as the total number of hours logged.

By Sarah Chellappa for The Conversation Our circadian rhythms are nearly 24-hour cycles that regulate alertness, hormones, body temperature

stories.title: Sleep regularity may outweigh duration
stories.summary: A study of 61,000 people suggests that maintaining a consistent sleep schedule may be a stronger indicator of long-term health than total hours slept. UC Berkeley scientist Matthew Walker notes that this regularity could be more significant than the traditional eight-hour rule. Consistency is the new duration.

stories.summary: High-Tech Sleep Health Metrics Weren't Connected To Better Performance , This Was In the last decade, wearables have promised insight into sleep efficiency, heart rate variability, and resting heart rate overnight. Many people use these metrics to predict performance, especially athletes and their coaches preparing

stories.title: FDA grants breakthrough status to pediatric insomnia drug
stories.summary: The FDA has granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation to daridorexant for treating insomnia in patients aged 10 to 18 years. A phase 2 study showed the drug increased total sleep time by 50 minutes. The company plans to begin a pediatric phase 3 clinical program next year.

stories.title: Sleep patterns may influence Alzheimer's progression
stories.summary: A study of 60 people found that specific sleep brainwaves were linked to lower levels of orexin, a chemical associated with faster mental decline in Alzheimer's patients. While the study cannot prove cause and effect, researchers are exploring whether better sleep activity could potentially slow the disease.

stories.title: Sleep analysis used to distinguish depression types
stories.summary: Investigators monitoring 159 adults found distinct sleep patterns between those with unipolar and bipolar depression. Using actigraphy and polysomnography, the study tracked participants over several years to identify differences in sleep quality and insomnia severity. The groups did not differ in age, sex, or depression severity.

stories.summary: Walking, strength, balance, flexibility and a slower pace: the routine of the woman who made aerobics famous. stories.title: Longevity study on meat consumption
stories.summary: A study suggesting meat eaters live to 100 has been widely shared. Researchers clarify the data reflects the risks of low protein and calorie intake in fragile, elderly populations rather than a general endorsement of meat. The findings serve as a warning, not a diet plan.

stories.title: Food refusal in young children
stories.summary: A Hyderabad study found nearly nine in 10 children aged 2 to 7 resist unfamiliar foods. Researchers suggest parents often mistake normal developmental behaviour for disobedience. The team recommends repeated exposure and pressure-free mealtimes to address food neophobia, noting that parental reaction plays a significant role.

stories.title: Grocery costs and mental health
stories.summary: Rising grocery prices are linked to increased food insufficiency and worsening mental health, according to a Penn State study using U.S. Census Bureau data. The analysis suggests that economic disruptions from the pandemic continue to affect how households manage their food spending and overall well-being.

stories.title: Gut health drives plant-based dairy demand
stories.summary: A Danone survey of 42,000 adults found that gut health is the primary driver for plant-based dairy consumption. The company suggests this creates an opportunity for fibre-enriched, GLP-1-friendly alternatives. Consumers appear more interested in how products feel to their digestion than the taste of oat milk.

stories.title: Full-fat dairy study results
stories.summary: A University of Toronto study found that three daily servings of full-fat dairy did not worsen weight, cholesterol, or insulin resistance over 12 weeks. Researchers observed improvements in blood pressure and nutrient intake. Longstanding advice to avoid full-fat dairy may now be subject to further review.

stories.title: Longevity supplement trial results
stories.summary: A placebo-controlled trial found that the supplement NOVOS Core was associated with improved artery function and systolic blood pressure in people around age 60. Researchers noted that blood lipids remained unaffected. It is currently unknown which specific ingredients in the combination product are responsible for the effects.

stories.title: Weight management and cognitive decline
stories.summary: A study suggests that managing weight may help slow cognitive decline as people age. While some brain changes are natural, researchers indicate that maintaining a healthy weight could be a factor in preserving cognitive function and reducing the risk of severe disorders over time.

stories.title: Fatty15 longevity supplement claims
stories.summary: The supplement Fatty15 is marketed as a way to support metabolic health and healthy aging, powered by the fatty acid C15:0. The brand describes it as the first essential fatty acid discovered in 90 years. It claims to work deep within cells to improve sleep and health.

stories.title: Gut bacteria and human aging
stories.summary: A study in Nature analyzed over 11,000 stool samples to identify genetic variants in gut bacteria. Researchers found 940 genetic associations linked to health characteristics and environmental factors. These findings suggest that gut microbiome genetics may offer new insights into the biological processes of human aging.

stories.title: Pandemic stress and adolescent aging
stories.summary: A study published in PNAS suggests that pandemic-related stress may have accelerated biological aging in adolescents. Researchers used epigenetic clocks to examine DNA methylation, finding measurable changes in gene activity. The study indicates that social isolation may have left a lasting impact on the bodies of teenagers.

stories.title: Study Links Breast Milk Fatty Acids to Infant Motor Development
stories.summary: A new study has found an association between odd- and branched-chain fatty acid (OBCFA) levels in breast milk and infant motor development, providing new population-based evidence for research on early-life nutrition and neurodevelopment. The study, published in European Journal of Nutrition on October 31, was

stories.title: VetCompass Study Unveils Health Demography and Lifespan of UK Shih Tzus
stories.summary: A comprehensive epidemiological investigation utilizing clinical records from the VetCompass Programme has characterized the demography, common disorder prevalence, and mortality patterns of Shih Tzu dogs receiving primary veterinary care across the United Kingdom. Drawing from an overall surveillance cohort of 336,865 dogs attending primary-care veterinary

stories.title: Rising food prices linked to mental health concerns
stories.summary: Researchers at Pennsylvania State University linked rising US food prices to increased household spending, food insufficiency, and poorer mental health indicators. The study, published in Applied Economic Perspectives and Policy, utilized data from the US Census Bureau. Financial stress appears to have a measurable psychological cost.

stories.title: Fatty15 marketed as longevity supplement
stories.summary: Fatty15 is marketed as a longevity supplement powered by C15:0, which the brand describes as the first essential fatty acid discovered in over 90 years. The company claims it works within cells to improve sleep and health. It is backed by more than 100 peer-reviewed studies.

stories.title: AYUSH medicines fail quality tests in Gujarat
stories.summary: Twenty-one samples of AYUSH medicines manufactured in Gujarat failed quality tests and were declared not of standard quality. The findings were presented in the Rajya Sabha, highlighting safety concerns as interest in traditional medicine systems grows. The state remains a major pharmaceutical manufacturing hub.

stories.title: Kerala integrates Ayurveda into resort stays
stories.summary: Kerala continues to promote its reputation as a destination for Ayurveda, with resorts now incorporating wellness centres into their grounds. Visitors can combine traditional treatments with a hotel stay. The model allows guests to access personalised wellness programmes while maintaining the pace of a luxury holiday.

stories.title: Netmeds links Diwali to Ayurvedic beauty
stories.summary: Netmeds suggests using Ayurveda for a self-cleansing beauty journey during Diwali. The platform describes the ancient science as a path to beauty that enhances outward appearance while uplifting the spirit. The festival is presented as an opportunity to reflect on holistic healing and inner glow.

stories.title: PM Modi highlights Ayurveda and preventive healthcare
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi shared an article written by Prataprao Jadhav. The piece focuses on the role of Ayurveda within the broader context of preventive healthcare in India. The government continues to promote traditional systems as a component of national health strategy.

stories.title: Dhanteras observed as birth anniversary of Lord Dhanvantari
stories.summary: Dhanteras is traditionally associated with new purchases and prosperity, but it is also observed as Dhanvantari Jayanti. Lord Dhanvantari is regarded as the divine physician and the god of Ayurveda. The festival links the act of shopping to the celebration of health and traditional medicine.

stories.title: Electroacupuncture study explores molecular effects in rats
stories.summary: Researchers at Fujian University of Traditional Chinese Medicine studied how electroacupuncture affects chronic atrophic gastritis in rats. The technique, which delivers electrical current through needles, has been reported to improve symptoms. The study aimed to identify the molecular mechanisms behind these observed changes in stomach tissue.

stories.title: Maharashtra FDA seizes hair oil over regrowth claims
stories.summary: The Maharashtra FDA seized 5,040 bottles of VS Hair Growth Oil worth Rs 50.34 lakh from a Nashik salon. The action was taken under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. The product was marketed with claims of regrowing hair on bald heads, which regulators deemed misleading.

stories.title: Maharashtra FDA seizes hair oil stock
stories.summary: The Maharashtra FDA seized 5,040 bottles of Ayurvedic hair oil worth Rs 50.35 lakh following allegations of misleading hair regrowth claims. The product was advertised on social media as a solution for baldness. Inspections were conducted at a salon and imitation jewellery business in Nashik.

stories.title: Financial dispute resolved for Ayurveda institute project
stories.summary: The Goa State Environment Impact Assessment Authority resolved a dispute regarding the All India Institute of Ayurveda campus in Pernem. Authorities decided no further payment is required for a disputed Rs 1.12 crore fee. The issue followed an audit regarding construction without prior environmental clearance.
